title: How long is XY at three different positions of X and Y?
description: The length XY is measured with a ruler for three positions of the two moving points, and each length is read in centimetres and millimetres. Keeko's doubt is that XY is seven centimetres every time.
teaching_notes: One idea: XY is exactly seven centimetres only when X and Y are level, and a bigger difference in height gives a longer XY. Watch for students who think XY is seven centimetres whatever the positions.

source: Rectangle ABCD has AB = 7 cm, BC = 4 cm. Measure XY and fill
video_script.why: A learner measures XY for three positions of X and Y and reads each length in centimetres and millimetres.
video_script.substitution: the book's own rectangle with AB seven centimetres and BC four centimetres, and the three positions of X and Y it lists
video_script.anchor: a rectangle with points X and Y placed by their distances from A and B, and a ruler laid along XY
video_script.wrong_answer: ex why is seven centimetres every time
video_script.wrong_move: reads XY as seven centimetres in every position without measuring the slanting ones
video_script.payoff_line: Ex why measures a little over seven centimetres, and exactly seven when level.

final_answer.value: a) 7 cm 4 mm, b) 7 cm 0 mm, c) 7 cm 3 mm

maths_rules: case a: X 5 mm from A, Y 3 cm from B; heights differ by 2 cm 5 mm; XY measures about 7 cm 4 mm
case b: X 1 cm from A, Y 1 cm from B; level, so XY = 7 cm 0 mm
case c: X 2 cm from A, Y 4 cm from B; heights differ by 2 cm; XY measures about 7 cm 3 mm
video_script.design: Three positions are placed one after the other, with a ruler laid along XY and the reading shown in centimetres and millimetres.

beats.on_screen: title card, then rectangle ABCD with X close to A on one side and Y high up on the opposite side

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the rectangle is drawn
marks.ask: X and Y appear and are joined by a slanting line

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about measuring ex why.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Here ex is close to eigh, while why is high up the opposite side.
Will ex why be more than seven centimetres, or less?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a ruler laid along XY with the reading in cm and mm; 10 mm = 1 cm

marks.place: ex and why are placed by their distances from eigh and bee
marks.read: the ruler reading is split into centimetres and millimetres

narration: <bookmark mark='place'/>We place ex and why by their distances up the sides from eigh and bee.
<bookmark mark='read'/>Then we lay a ruler along ex why and read the centimetres and the millimetres.
Ten millimetres make one centimetre.

beats.on_screen: Given: AB = 7 cm, BC = 4 cm; three positions of X and Y
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, eigh bee is seven centimetres and bee cee is four centimetres.

beats.on_screen: To find: the length XY in each of the three positions

marks.find: the question is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to measure ex why in three positions.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: X is 5 mm from A, Y is 3 cm from B; XY measures 7 cm 4 mm

marks.pos: X is placed 5 mm up from A and Y is placed 3 cm up from B
marks.meas: the ruler reading 7 cm 4 mm appears

narration: <bookmark mark='pos'/>Step one, ex is five millimetres from eigh, and why is three centimetres from bee.
<bookmark mark='meas'/>Ex why measures seven centimetres four millimetres.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: X is 1 cm from A, Y is 1 cm from B; XY measures 7 cm 0 mm

marks.pos: X and Y are placed level, 1 cm up
marks.meas: the ruler reading 7 cm 0 mm appears

narration: <bookmark mark='pos'/>Step two, ex is one centimetre from eigh, and why is one centimetre from bee.
<bookmark mark='meas'/>They are level, and ex why measures seven centimetres zero millimetres.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: X is 2 cm from A, Y is 4 cm from B; XY measures 7 cm 3 mm

marks.pos: X is placed 2 cm up from A and Y is placed 4 cm up from B
marks.meas: the ruler reading 7 cm 3 mm appears

narration: <bookmark mark='pos'/>Step three, ex is two centimetres from eigh, and why is four centimetres from bee.
<bookmark mark='meas'/>Ex why measures seven centimetres three millimetres.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 7 cm 4 mm, 7 cm 0 mm, 7 cm 3 mm

marks.res: the three readings are listed in a row

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Ex why measures a little over seven centimetres, and exactly seven when level.
<bookmark mark='res'/>The three lengths are seven centimetres four millimetres, seven centimetres zero millimetres, and seven centimetres three millimetres.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the three readings
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: the three readings side by side; the level one is exactly 7 cm and the slanting ones are longer

marks.doubt: the three readings appear with the word every time crossed out
marks.fix: the level reading is circled as exactly 7 cm
marks.keep: the two slanting readings are circled as longer

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks ex why is seven centimetres every time.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But ex why is exactly seven only when the two points are level.
<bookmark mark='keep'/>When one point is higher, the line slants, and a bigger difference in height gives a longer line.
